## Task
Given this project's tech stack and testing approach, generate an isolation config for concurrent workers.
Each worker runs in a separate git worktree and needs its own test environment.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object: { "setup": "<shell command>", "verify": "<shell command>", "teardown": "<shell command>", "env": { "KEY": "value" } }
Use ${TASK_ID} as a placeholder for the unique worker identifier.
Examples:
  iOS: { "setup": "xcrun simctl clone 'iPhone 16' 'worker-${TASK_ID}'", "verify": "xcrun simctl list | grep 'worker-${TASK_ID}'", "teardown": "xcrun simctl delete 'worker-${TASK_ID}'" }
  Web: { "setup": "createdb test_${TASK_ID}", "verify": "pg_isready -d test_${TASK_ID}", "teardown": "dropdb test_${TASK_ID}" }
  If no isolation is needed (e.g., tests use unique temp dirs by default), respond: { "setup": "true", "verify": "true", "teardown": "true" }

## Swarm Context
--- swarm: core/style.md (core) ---
# Style

- Match the conventions of the surrounding code before introducing new ones.
- Prefer small, focused changes. One change per commit, with a message that says why.
- Name things for what they do. Avoid abbreviations a new reader would have to look up.
- Delete dead code instead of commenting it out.
- Handle errors where they can be acted on, and say what failed and what to do next.


--- swarm: core/testing.md (core) ---
# Testing

- Every behaviour change ships with a test that fails without it.
- Test behaviour through the public interface, not private helpers.
- Keep tests independent: no shared mutable state, no reliance on run order.
- Use temporary directories and fake clocks instead of the real filesystem and time.
- A flaky test is a bug. Fix the cause; do not add retries.

# Docs

- Write for the reader who arrives with a task: lead with what to do, then why.
- Keep examples runnable and copy-pasteable, and keep them in sync with the code.

## Task
Analyze this goal and break it down into specific, actionable implementation tasks.

## Goal: add a Requirements section to the README stating that Node.js 26 or newer runs src/index.ts directly

## Acceptance Criteria
- README.md has a Requirements section that names Node.js 26 or newer
- The existing README sections are kept

## Constraints
- Do not change src/index.ts or package.json

## Instructions
Explore the project codebase to understand the current state.
Then output a JSON object containing a "shared_files" array and a "tasks" array. Each task should be a specific, concrete action.
For each task, provide a short "title" (under 60 chars, like a commit subject) and a longer "description" that explains what to do.
Order them by dependency — tasks that must happen first should come first.
Mark independent tasks with "parallel": true.

For each task, declare ALL files it will touch — including secondary files:
- "creates": files this task will create that do not exist yet. Use full relative paths from the project root.
- "modifies": existing files this task will need to change. Use full relative paths from the project root.
This is used to detect conflicts between parallel tasks. When unsure whether a task will modify a file, include it in "modifies" — over-declaring is safe (slower but prevents conflicts), under-declaring risks expensive merge conflicts.

CRITICAL: Most merge conflicts happen on shared files that tasks touch as side effects. For EVERY task, think about:
- Route/endpoint registration files (e.g., routes/index.ts, app.ts)
- Barrel/index exports (e.g., src/index.ts, models/index.ts)
- Config files (e.g., package.json, tsconfig.json)
- Middleware chains, validation schemas, shared type definitions
- Dependency manifests, app entry points
If a task creates a new file, it almost certainly also modifies an index/barrel file to export it.

Also identify "shared_files" — files that MULTIPLE tasks will need to modify. These will be auto-injected into each task's "modifies" to prevent conflicts.

## CRITICAL — Output Format
You may explore the codebase first (list directories, read files) to understand the project structure.
After exploring, your FINAL response MUST be ONLY a JSON object — no prose, no markdown, no explanation before or after the JSON.
The JSON will be machine-parsed. Any text outside the JSON will cause a parse failure.

Required JSON format:
```json
{
  "shared_files": ["src/routes/index.ts", "src/app.ts"],
  "tasks": [
    { "title": "Short task title", "description": "Detailed explanation of what to do and why", "intent": "investigation|implementation|code-review", "parallel": false, "creates": ["src/new-file.ts"], "modifies": ["src/index.ts"] },
    { "title": "Another task title", "description": "Detailed steps for this task", "intent": "implementation", "parallel": true, "creates": [], "modifies": ["src/index.ts", "src/routes/index.ts"] }
  ]
}
```
